brief_problem: Splitting the bill at the canteen

runs.text: A useful program does not carry its data written inside: it asks for it every time it runs.
The problem
A group of friends eats at the canteen. A
tip is added to the bill and it is split in equal parts. Since nobody carries coins, each one pays a
whole
number of pesos, rounding up so that it is enough. The bill and the number of friends change every time.
How much does each one pay?
Try it
Work out by hand how much each one pays if the bill is 120 pesos and there are 4 friends.
The tip is a tenth of 120: 12. The total is 132. Among 4 friends, each one pays
Understand
This time the person who writes the program does not know the data: the person who uses it knows them, at the canteen. Before thinking about instructions it pays to write the problem on a
problem card
: what goes in, what comes out, how they relate and several worked examples.

blocks.description: A card with four zones for the tip problem: the bill and the number of friends go in; what each one pays comes out; the relation says how the total is computed and shared; the worked examples are 120 and 4 giving 33, 100 and 3 giving 37, and 100 and 1 giving 110.

caption.text: The card is filled in before writing. If you cannot fill in a zone, you have not understood the problem yet.

relation.text: the total is the bill plus a tenth of it; each one pays the total divided among the friends, rounded up.

runs.text: Test
Look at the second one: three friends pay 37 each, 111 in total, one peso more than the bill. Rounding up always leaves a bit extra, and that is exactly what the problem asked for.
Improve
In one sentence:
The program asks for the bill and the friends, and says how much each one pays with the tip included
An awkward question remains: what if someone types 0 friends? Do not run it yet; it is the problem of the next lesson.
What you learned
